question: Can Drive files.download return a valid native Google Sheets XLSX export larger than the 10 MiB files.export ceiling from one run-owned Shared Drive fixture?
kind: Pre-registered bounded live functional probe. One item and one run do not establish general large-export reliability.
authorization: The owner authorized creation of dedicated Shared Drive test objects for Cirrove validation. Create only one uniquely named native Sheet inside the existing Cirrove Validation folder; retain its exact private identity for follow-up. Do not touch existing user items.
arms: A: confirm the exact selected Shared Drive and test folder, create one new run-owned native Sheet, and save its exact item ID privately before content upload

B: import a deterministic approximately 28 MiB two-column CSV with 70,000 data rows into only that new item; make no blind retry after an uncertain response and inspect exact metadata before proceeding

C: request XLSX through files.download LRO with explicit MIME and bounded polling, authenticate the Google-owned download origin, strip auth on redirects, require a valid ZIP with workbook/sheet XML, at least 10 MiB of bytes, known marker cells, and unchanged source version across export
D: verify the installed original mounts remain ready with no failed uploads or stuck changes
endpoint: Pass only if the owned fixture export exceeds 10 MiB, all ZIP/content and identity checks pass, the source version stays stable, and original mounts remain healthy. A smaller artifact is inconclusive. On failure retain the fixture and private evidence; never retry an uncertain upload blindly.
prediction: The approximately 28 MiB high-entropy CSV should produce an XLSX over 10 MiB and files.download should return it without the files.export cap. Import/conversion latency is uncertain.
limits: One artificially large Sheet does not prove user-document fidelity, arbitrary MIME formats, long polling, token expiry handling, memory bounds inside Cirrove, or production reliability.

result.interpretation: A direct read-only Drive files.download LRO returned a valid 22,344,729-byte XLSX for one run-owned Workspace Sheet, exceeding files.export’s documented 10 MiB limit. This supports an adapter implementation but does not test Cirrove’s mounted path.

export_limit_control: Read-only GET files.export for the exact large run-owned Sheet and XLSX MIME; record only HTTP status and bounded structured reason, no response body. This control demonstrates the current transport’s behavior on the same item; it does not modify the LRO result.

export_limit_control_result.interpretation: The currently implemented files.export path rejects this test artifact, while files.download returned 22,344,729 valid XLSX bytes. No raw error body was retained.
